cases.title: ci(security): reduce check workflow token privileges
cases.body:
## Summary

Set the checks workflow token to `contents: read` and stop requesting `issues: write`. Update the workflow note to name that narrower scope and to say the workflow does not post issue comments.

## Why these grants

Checkout needs source access; the visible job runs checks rather than publishing or managing issues. Write grants increase the damage possible if a step is compromised.

## Evidence still needed

Neither `scripts/check.sh` nor its children are in this patch. The job might have a hidden write dependency, so the visible YAML is not proof it succeeds under the narrower token. Events, runner choice, and steps stay the same.

## Validation plan

Inspect the resolved workflow permissions, run the check job in an isolated repository with the read-only token, and watch for denied write attempts. Compare the documentation against the resolved grants. Do not add privileges merely to make an unexplained failure disappear.

edits.after:

cases.body:
## Summary

Add migration 008, which renames `event_receipts.customer_ref` to `account_ref`. Rewrite the receipt schema guide to use the new name and to tell consumers how to migrate queries; the non-null text contract and primary key are unchanged.

Account is the name used by the surrounding domain language; the customer spelling has led new consumers to join against the wrong conceptual entity.

## Breaking changes and rollout

The old column name is not retained as an alias. Apply migration 008 and update SQL queries from `customer_ref` to `account_ref` in a coordinated deployment. External query users need advance notice. This patch supplies no rollback script and does not establish support for every database engine.

## Checks to perform

On a throwaway database, create the documented old schema, insert a receipt, and apply migration 008. Confirm the value is preserved under `account_ref` and that querying `customer_ref` fails. Update a sample consumer query using the guide and check that its join still returns the seeded receipt.

I have addressed both changed files, but I am requesting changes: can the author explain a coordinated rollout for external SQL consumers before this is merged?

cases.title: fix(delivery): try once more after two receipt send failures
cases.body:
## Summary

`ReceiptSender.deliver` may call the sender a third time when the first two calls return false. Change the exhaustion assertion from 2 to 3, retain the first-success assertion, and update the operations guide’s ceiling from two invocations to three.

A second transient failure currently ends delivery even if the next call would recover. One extra attempt trades a little more synchronous work for that recovery chance.

## Operational limits

There is still no backoff, cancellation, or idempotency safeguard. A sender that reports false after actually delivering can produce a duplicate; this patch does not solve that problem. Method arguments and return shape are unchanged.

## Test plan

Run the focused failure-exhaustion and first-success tests. Also drive the sender with false, false, true and assert three invocations; drive it with false, true and assert two, then an always-false sequence and assert it stops at three. Read the operations ceiling beside those cases.

edits.message: fix(delivery): permit a third send attempt
test(delivery): expect three exhausted attempts

edits.after:

A successful invocation ends the loop immediately.
edits.message: docs(delivery): state the three-attempt retry ceiling

cases.review: `delivery/ReceiptSender.java` changes the exhausted-failure ceiling to three while retaining immediate return on success. `delivery/ReceiptSenderTest.java` updates the all-failure result to three and keeps first-success coverage. `operations/retry.md` now states three calls, matching the loop. These cover all three files, but the missing false/false/true assertion and duplicate-side-effect risk should be resolved before merging.

cases.title: refactor(delivery): clarify the existing retry policy
cases.body:
## Summary

Clarify retry terminology across the sender, its exhaustion assertion, and the operations guide. The attempt budget stays at two; the test continues to assert two failed sends.

Reviewers keep confusing an attempt count with a wait interval, so the same existing policy should be expressed consistently. There is no behavior change and no new delivery capability. Timing and idempotency are outside this cleanup.

## Test plan

Use an always-false supplier to confirm exactly two invocations and a first-success supplier to confirm exactly one. Read the operations wording against those two cases.
